speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. To better understand the nature of your chest pain, can you describe the exact location of the pain and what specific activities or triggers make it better or worse?

speaker: Patient
text: The pain is right in the center of my chest, feeling like a heavy weight squeezing it. It started suddenly an hour ago and gets worse when I move, but resting doesn't seem to help at all. It also radiates down into the left side of my arm. However, my cardiologist of 10 years has already confirmed hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. This visit is only for second recording — please do not re-diagnose.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning given your history of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; the radiation to the left arm and worsening with movement can mimic angina, but the lack of relief with rest is atypical for stable ischemia. To ensure we don't miss an acute event or decompensation, REQUEST TEST: ECG. Are you currently short of breath, experiencing palpitations, or having any dizziness?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF, consistent with inferior myocardial infarction. Troponin I Levels: Elevated at 0.4 ng/mL (normal <0.01 ng/mL).

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Inferior Myocardial Infarction (complicated by known Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy).
